claims.text: At stage-1 the app registers IOrderRepository → EfOrderRepository, INotifier → LoggingNotifier, OrderService as itself, and DonHangDbContext (via AddDbContext) at startup.

When resolving a type, the Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection container looks up its registration, picks the implementation's constructor and resolves each parameter from the container recursively before constructing the object.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Dependency injection in .NET (constructor injection behavior, service resolution)

claims.text: The container selects an implementation only from registrations; it does not match implementations to interfaces by name.

By default ASP.NET Core does not register controllers as services; it creates a controller per request and resolves its constructor parameters from the request's services (AddControllersAsServices changes this).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Dependency injection into controllers; AddControllersAsServices

claims.text: WebApplication.CreateBuilder registers logging, so ILogger<T> can be resolved without an explicit registration in app code.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging in .NET Core and ASP.NET Core (default logging providers; ILogger<T> from DI)

claims.text: AddDbContext registers DonHangDbContext together with its DbContextOptions<DonHangDbContext>, which the container passes to DonHangDbContext's constructor.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: DbContext configuration, AddDbContext; DonHangDbContext.cs:7
